programme: TRIM28 (32/32) with ZBTB33 (Kaiso), EZH2 and SRCAP forms a repressive chromatin module: TRIM28/KAP1 nucleates H3K9 trimethylation through SETDB1, Kaiso reads methylated CpG, EZH2 supplies PRC2 H3K27 methylation, and SRCAP remodels nucleosomes by depositing H2A.Z. ZNF202 is a KRAB zinc finger, the class that recruits TRIM28, which strengthens the reading. NR4A3, MEF2D and ELF3 sit outside it.
role_in_a: Loss of heterochromatin integrity and derepression of normally silenced loci, including transposable elements, is a documented mechanism of tau-driven neurodegeneration, and TRIM28 has been implicated in tau and alpha-synuclein handling.
role_in_b: Uveal melanoma is driven by GNAQ/GNA11 with BAP1 loss, and BAP1 loss shifts the polycomb balance so that EZH2/PRC2-dependent silencing becomes a dependency of the aggressive class.
shared_axis: Both diseases turn on how tightly TRIM28- and PRC2-dependent silencing is maintained: derepression of heterochromatin in neurons, and a polycomb-dependent dedifferentiated state in BAP1-null melanoma. The same silencing machinery, moved in opposite directions.
reasoning: The module is coherent and specific - a KRAB-TRIM28-SETDB1 silencing complex plus PRC2 plus a KRAB zinc finger among the twelve - and TRIM28 is concordant in all 32 comparisons. I know of no documented link between Alzheimers disease and uveal melanoma through chromatin silencing, and neither anatomy nor clinical practice suggests one, which is what unexpected means here; it does not mean I take absence of literature as proof of novelty. Only 32 comparisons, so the recurrence is thin.
support: 24464041 — tau promotes neurodegeneration through global chromatin relaxation and derepression of heterochromatic loci.
how_to_falsify: The account predicts that loci held silent by TRIM28 and PRC2 are derepressed in Alzheimer's brain and silenced in BAP1-null uveal melanoma. If TRIM28 and H3K27me3 occupancy profiles in the two tissues share no such loci, the account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain | uvea. 32 patient-group combinations from 3 independent cohort pairs; the recurrence rests on few combinations.
